messages.subject: Urgent — HSE attending Wednesbury today after yesterday's incident
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

We had a serious incident at the Wednesbury plant yesterday afternoon. An operator, Wayne Tully, suffered a bad hand injury on one of the thread-rolling cells and is in hospital. We reported it under RIDDOR last night. An HSE inspector — Karen Whitlow — is coming to site this morning.

Can you call me as soon as you can? We need to know how to handle the inspection and the document requests. Andrew is keen we get ahead of this.

Patricia

Patricia Vaughan
General Counsel & Company Secretary
Calverton Industries Limited

messages.snippet: Patricia, I'm very sorry to hear this. Calling you in five minutes. In the meantime, the key points
messages.subject: RE: Urgent — HSE attending Wednesbury today after yesterday's incident
messages.plaintextBody:
Patricia,

I'm very sorry to hear this. Calling you in five minutes. In the meantime, the key points for today:

- Be cooperative and courteous with Inspector Whitlow but do not let anyone be interviewed under caution today without us present.
- Preserve everything: machine logs, the PLC/control data, CCTV, maintenance and training records, risk assessments. Suspend any routine deletion.
- Keep the cell isolated and locked off; don't disturb it beyond making it safe.
- Route document requests through us where you can.

Tom Gallagher will be your day-to-day contact and can be on site tomorrow. Engagement letter to follow.

Sarah

--
Sarah Whitfield
Partner | Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Strictly private and confidential.
